articles.title: The Plan: At the Windsor in Brooklyn’s Windsor Terrace, Assume Nothing
articles.narrative: Local Development Group has launched sales for The Windsor, a new condominium development in Brooklyn's Windsor Terrace neighborhood. The project offers 98 condominium units ranging from studios to three-bedrooms, priced between $525,000 and $1.67 million, alongside 33 affordable rental units. The developer aimed to create a building that blends with the neighborhood's classic aesthetic while providing luxury amenities, with move-ins anticipated to begin in October.

data_points.notable_features: Features 18,000 square feet of interconnected, WiFi-enabled indoor and outdoor amenity spaces including a pet spa, movie room, work-from-home suite, gym, children's playroom, and game lounge. Residences have 9-foot ceilings, oversize casement windows, wide-plank white oak flooring, buffed-stone countertops, and heated bathroom floors in condos. Approximately half of the condos include private outdoor space.
data_points.project_notes: Includes 33 rental units designated as affordable housing under the state's old 421-a tax abatement program. Sales launched in June 2026. Temporary certificate of occupancy expected within four to five weeks of publication.

articles.title: Meet the Broadway Brokers of New York Real Estate
articles.narrative: This article profiles several New York City real estate brokers who also have significant careers in Broadway theater, highlighting the transferable skills and shared characteristics between the two industries. Chloe Tucker Caine of SERHANT, set to debut in "Six," leverages her theatrical background to create musical listing videos and recently closed an $18 million condo sale. Brown Harris Stevens brokers Marsi Gardiner and Jordan Silver, both Tony Award-winning producers, emphasize the importance of relationships, creative problem-solving, and risk-taking in both real estate and theater. They note similarities in presenting a product to the right audience and the excitement of new opportunities.

articles.title: Starwood Advances 226K-SF Data Center in Fairfax County, Va.
articles.narrative: Starwood Capital Group is moving forward with the first phase of its Plaza 500 development in Fairfax County, Virginia, filing plans for a 226,469-square-foot data center. The initial construction phase for the building shell is estimated at $5 million. This project is part of a larger data center initiative by Starwood in Northern Virginia, which has faced community opposition regarding the proximity of a proposed electrical substation to residential areas.

data_points.notable_features: Two-story data center rising 75 feet.
data_points.project_notes: The 34-acre site was previously acquired for $165 million in 2022. Starwood is also awaiting approval for a proposed electrical substation.

articles.title: Real Estate Firm Yuco, AI Company Elite Each Take 7K SF at 757 Third Avenue
articles.narrative: Yuco Management, a real estate firm, and Elite, an AI-powered legal software company, each signed leases for 6,960 square feet at 757 Third Avenue in Midtown East. Yuco Management will relocate its offices to the 27th floor, while Elite will establish its first New York City office on the 22nd floor. The leases reflect strong Midtown leasing fundamentals and the value tenants place on well-executed repositioning strategies, according to the landlord's broker.

data_points.address: 757 Third Avenue, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Class A office building, 26 stories, located two blocks east of Grand Central Terminal.
data_points.project_notes: New York Life Real Estate Investors acquired the property in October 2025 through a deed-in-lieu of foreclosure sale and is undertaking cosmetic renovations to the lobby and rolling out a new prebuilt office program.

articles.title: Rosewood Begins Leasing 359-Unit Multifamily Project in San Antonio
articles.narrative: Rosewood Property Co. has commenced leasing for a 359-unit multifamily project in San Antonio, marking Phase III of the Tobin Estates development. The project offers a mix of traditional apartments and units with private garages, featuring a range of floor plans and amenities such as a pool, fitness centers, and a rooftop deck. The development began construction in May 2024.

data_points.notable_features: Units include one-, two-, and three-bedroom floor plans, with amenities such as a pool, indoor and outdoor fitness centers, a resident lounge, and a rooftop deck. 94 units feature private garages.
data_points.project_notes: Construction began in May 2024. This project is Phase III of the larger Tobin Estates development.

articles.title: HLCI Completes 254,186 SF Industrial Project in Northwest Houston
articles.narrative: Holt Lunsford Commercial Investments (HLCI) has completed Par 1960, a two-building industrial project totaling 254,186 square feet in northwest Houston. The development, which began construction in late 2024, offers modern industrial space with varying clear heights and loading configurations across its two buildings. Cushman & Wakefield has been appointed as the leasing agent for the property.

data_points.notable_features: Building 1 spans 204,375 square feet with 32-foot clear heights and a front-load configuration. Building 2 totals 49,811 square feet with 28-foot clear heights and a rear-load configuration.
data_points.project_notes: Construction began in late 2024.

articles.title: Cooler Master Corp. Signs 97,285 SF Industrial Lease in West Houston
articles.narrative: Cooler Master Corp. has signed a 97,285-square-foot industrial lease for the entirety of Building 2 within the Grand West Crossing development in West Houston. This transaction represents a significant commitment to the area, as Grand West Crossing is a multi-phase project with additional buildings under construction, indicating ongoing industrial growth in the market.

data_points.project_notes: Building 2 is part of the Grand West Crossing development, which is planned to include six buildings, with two completed and two under construction.

articles.title: Red Rock to Develop 519,792 SF Industrial Facility Near Columbia, South Carolina
articles.narrative: Red Rock Developments is set to construct a 519,792-square-foot speculative industrial facility within the Sandy Run Industrial Park in Gaston, a suburb of Columbia, South Carolina. The cross-dock facility will feature 40-foot clear heights and 98 dock-high doors, with groundbreaking anticipated this quarter. Colliers has been retained to handle the marketing and leasing of the property.

data_points.notable_features: Cross-dock facility with 40-foot clear heights, 185-foot truck courts, 98 dock-high doors, four drive-in doors, ESFR sprinkler system, and expandable parking.
data_points.project_notes: The facility will be built on a speculative basis within the 760-acre Sandy Run Industrial Park.

articles.title: Small Parcels, Big Demand: How O’Hare keeps outperforming Chicago’s industrial market
articles.narrative: The O'Hare industrial submarket in Chicago continues to outperform the broader metropolitan industrial market, driven by a scarcity of large development parcels that limits new supply. This constraint keeps vacancy rates low, around 5.4-5.5%, compared to 8.5-9% in the wider suburban market. Demand is concentrated in smaller industrial spaces, typically 10,000 to 50,000 square feet, attracting air freight, pharmaceutical, and last-mile logistics users who value the central location. Brokers anticipate that rents will remain high and continue to grow due to persistent demand and the lack of developable land, with new supply focusing on infill locations and leveraging favorable tax treatment.

articles.title: Colliers negotiates 56,760-square-foot headquarters lease in Chicago
articles.narrative: Swanson, Martin & Bell, LLP, a law firm, has restructured and renewed its long-term headquarters lease for 56,760 square feet at 330 N. Wabash Ave. in Chicago. The firm, which has grown significantly since its founding, will continue to occupy space in the iconic 52-story office tower, which is notable as the last building designed by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe in the U.S.

data_points.notable_features: The 52-story office tower was the last building in the U.S. designed by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, featuring 35,000 SF floor plates, floor-to-ceiling windows, 12' ceilings, panoramic city views, and direct access to the Chicago Riverwalk.

articles.title: What to look for in a snow removal plan
articles.narrative: This article provides facility managers with key considerations for developing a comprehensive snow removal plan. It emphasizes the importance of defining desired outcomes and levels of service rather than focusing solely on equipment. The author highlights the need for plans to address varying weather conditions, manage meltwater and snow pile placement, ensure continuous accessibility routes, and clearly delineate decision-making authority. Additionally, the article stresses the importance of matching equipment to property limitations and implementing a strategic material application approach, advocating for detailed documentation and adherence to industry standards.

articles.title: What’s Good For Texas is Good For the Midwest
articles.market: St. Louis, MO / Kansas City, MO
articles.narrative: SparrowHawk, a Houston-based industrial real estate firm, secured $300 million in growth capital from Almanac Realty Investors to expand its portfolio and platform, particularly in the Midwest markets of St. Louis and Kansas City. The firm also bolstered its senior leadership team with the appointments of Scott Brast as Senior Vice President of Investments and Capital Markets, and Peter Wismer as Senior Vice President of Finance and Financial Reporting. These strategic moves are intended to accelerate SparrowHawk's growth as a premier industrial investment platform, capitalizing on strong market fundamentals driven by e-commerce, reshoring, and supply chain modernization.

articles.title: Brookfield picks up stake in Healthpeak’s $2B medical office venture
articles.narrative: Brookfield Asset Management has acquired a 49% stake in Healthpeak Properties' $2.1 billion medical office portfolio, forming a joint venture for the 86-property, 5.6 million-square-foot portfolio. Healthpeak retains a 51% controlling interest and will manage the venture, receiving over $1 billion in proceeds. This transaction provides long-term capital for the portfolio, which is 95% leased with a weighted average lease term of six years, and allows Healthpeak to advance its capital allocation priorities by leveraging strong demand for outpatient care.

data_points.notable_features: Portfolio spans nearly a dozen states, including Illinois, New York, and New Jersey, with a weighted average of six years remaining on leases.

articles.title: Boxabl ignites SPAC market, goes public at $3.5B valuation
articles.narrative: Boxabl, a Las Vegas-based modular housing startup, has gone public on the Nasdaq after completing its merger with special purpose acquisition company FG Merger II Corp. The transaction, which valued the combined entity at $3.5 billion, will provide Boxabl with increased access to capital to expand its production and development of prefabricated building systems. The company, known for its "Casita" tiny homes, aims to scale its operations following the public listing.

articles.title: Lake Havasu new build sets local price record nearly two years after listing
articles.narrative: A newly constructed lakeside estate in Lake Havasu City, Arizona, has sold for $4.5 million, establishing a new record for residential property sales in the area. The 6,000-square-foot luxury home, developed by Gaskin Design and Development, was initially listed for $6.7 million in December 2024 before its price reduction. The sale highlights the evolving dynamics of the luxury housing market in the region, even as the broader Phoenix metro area experiences significant home price reductions.

data_points.address: 2437 Wren Cove Way, Lake Havasu City, AZ
data_points.notable_features: Four bedrooms, four and a half bathrooms, 14-foot vaulted ceilings, Italian porcelain flooring, and a 500-bottle wine room.
data_points.project_notes: Located in the gated Riviera Lake Havasu community. This was the developer's first build in the area, which includes 10 lots.

companies_people.label: SELLER BROKER
companies_people.firm_name: Grigg's Group Powered by the Altman Brothers

articles.market_intelligence: Metro Phoenix ranked first nationwide in home price cuts in April. The median home price in Lake Havasu City is approximately $500,000. Arizona ranks eighth in the country in home sales per capita.

articles.title: NYC’s top deals: Noho apartment building trades for $17M
articles.narrative: Aston of Bowry LLC has acquired a four-story apartment building located at 312 Bowery in NoHo for $16.7 million. The property, previously owned by Bremen House Inc., features 22 residential units across nearly 22,500 square feet. This transaction represents the highest-priced commercial sale recorded in New York City during the reporting period.

articles.title: Citywide ballot measures pitch faster permitting, procurement
articles.narrative: New York City's Commission on Government Efficiency (COGE) is proposing several ballot measures to streamline the city's permitting and procurement processes, aiming to accelerate construction and contract awards. Key proposals include establishing a central hub for construction permits across multiple agencies, delegating certificate of occupancy authority, and centralizing waterfront permitting under the Department of Buildings. Additionally, measures are proposed to simplify the procurement of goods and services for small businesses and nonprofits, and to expedite the repurposing of small public land lots and the leasing of office space for municipal use. These changes are intended to support the Mamdani administration's goal of creating and preserving 400,000 affordable housing units over the next decade by reducing bureaucratic delays.

companies_people.firm_name: New York State Association for Affordable Housing

articles.title: 295 Fifth Ave owners push for revival with refinancing
articles.narrative: A joint venture between PGIM, Tribeca Investment Group, and Meadow Partners secured a $228.9 million floating-rate, interest-only bridge loan to refinance 295 Fifth Avenue, also known as the Textile Building, in Midtown South. The refinancing follows a $350 million capital improvement project that added significant amenities and a penthouse to the 19-story office building. Despite the building being 50 percent leased, the owners are reportedly on a path to stabilization, with notable tenants having recently signed leases.

data_points.address: 295 Fifth Avenue, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: 19-story office building with a ground-floor courtyard, several terraces, hospitality amenities, and a two-story penthouse.
data_points.project_notes: The sponsorship group previously secured $150 million in debt in November 2022. A $350 million capital improvements project was undertaken.

articles.market_intelligence: Midtown South accounted for nearly 45 percent of all leasing demand in Manhattan in April, securing four of the borough's five largest office leases. Manhattan's leasing activity saw 11 million square feet taken in Q2 and a first-half total of 22.8 million square feet, potentially making it the busiest leasing year since 2000.

articles.title: Turret takes over debt on troubled Upper East Side condo buildings
articles.narrative: Turret Equities has acquired a distressed $19.9 million debt note secured by two condo buildings on the Upper East Side of Manhattan. The current owner, Continuum Analytics, had defaulted on its loans and was facing foreclosure by the original lender, Preferred Bank. This acquisition expands Turret's portfolio of distressed debt in the Upper East Side market.

data_points.address: 184 East 64th Street / 227 East 67th Street, New York City, NY
data_points.project_notes: The buildings were previously purchased by Preferred Bank at a bankruptcy auction in February 2019 for $32.5 million and sold to Continuum Analytics two months later for $38 million. Preferred Bank also provided Continuum with a $29 million loan and refinanced the properties with a nearly $20 million loan in 2023.

articles.title: BXP putting 7 Times Square ground lease on the market
articles.narrative: BXP is marketing the ground lease for 7 Times Square, a 1.2 million-square-foot office tower in Manhattan, with an asking price between $700 million and $750 million. The offering, which could pertain to BXP's majority stake or the entire ground lease, represents one of the few single-property office deals at this price point in recent years. The property, developed in 2004 and currently 91% leased, includes recent amenity upgrades and generates additional revenue from electronic billboards.

data_points.address: 7 Times Square, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Features four floors of electronic billboards, providing an additional revenue source. Recent amenity additions include conference space, a client lounge, and cafe services.
data_points.project_notes: The property is on a 99-year ground lease with the city, which includes an option to purchase. Norges Bank Investment Management acquired a 45% stake in the property for $684 million in 2013.

articles.market_intelligence: Since 2020, only nine single-property office deals in the U.S. have crossed the $700 million threshold, according to Green Street's Sale Comps Database.

articles.title: Braemar sells Key West resort amid Ashford split
articles.narrative: Braemar Hotels & Resorts has agreed to sell the oceanfront Pier House Resort & Spa in Key West for $190 million, or $1.3 million per key. The 142-key hotel, which Braemar acquired in 2014 for $93 million, is being sold to an undisclosed buyer as part of a broader asset disposition strategy. This sale, along with other luxury hotel dispositions, is intended to fund a $480 million termination fee associated with Braemar's separation from its long-time manager, Ashford Incorporated, as the REIT transitions to a self-managed structure.

data_points.notable_features: Oceanfront resort.
data_points.project_notes: Braemar acquired the property for $93 million in 2014 after a $12 million renovation.

articles.title: Related Urban targets aging Coconut Grove housing for two-tower project
articles.narrative: Related Urban Development Group has filed plans for Magnus Grove and Stirrup Plaza, a two-tower multifamily project in Coconut Grove, Miami. The development aims to replace aging public housing with 750 new apartments, including affordable housing units under Florida's Live Local Act, along with retail, a library, and parking. This project aligns with Related Urban's strategy of partnering with Miami-Dade County to modernize public housing sites with higher-density, mixed-income developments, despite local opposition to the Live Local Act.

data_points.address: 3150 and 3160 Mundy Street and 3181 Douglas Road, Miami, FL
data_points.notable_features: Includes 7,300 square feet of retail, a 7,650-square-foot library, and a 796-space parking garage. Located within Miami-Dade’s Rapid Transit Zone near the Douglas Road Metrorail Station.
data_points.project_notes: Project seeks to demolish a 100-unit apartment building (built 1975) and a 65-unit building (built 1982), while preserving a 68-unit apartment building and a standalone wellness center. At least 40 percent of units must be offered at below-market rates to qualify for the Live Local Act.

articles.title: Witkoff, Monroe Capital score $303M loan for huge Miami Worldcenter project
articles.narrative: Witkoff and Monroe Capital secured a $302.6 million construction loan for the first phase of their large-scale residential and retail project at Miami Worldcenter. The financing, provided by Athene Annuity and Life Company and J.P. Morgan Chase, includes $245.3 million in new construction funding and refinances $57.3 million in existing debt. The initial phase will feature an 894-unit residential tower, over 17,000 square feet of retail, and a nine-story parking garage, marking a significant step in the development of one of Miami Worldcenter's last major undeveloped parcels.

data_points.notable_features: Kobi Karp-designed project within Miami Worldcenter, one of the district's final large-scale undeveloped parcels.
data_points.project_notes: The 5-acre development site was previously acquired for $94 million in 2021. The project will ultimately include 2,346 residential units, 30,500 square feet of commercial space, and 2,078 parking spaces across four towers. The transaction refinanced $57.3 million in existing debt and provided $245.3 million in new construction financing.

articles.title: Big Tech, big offices: Google supersizes Miami presence on heels of Larry Page, Sergey Brin’s resi spree
articles.narrative: Alphabet, Google's parent company, has significantly expanded its office footprint in Miami, quadrupling its space at the 1450 Brickell Avenue tower to approximately 45,000 square feet. This expansion, which closed in the spring, signals a serious commitment by major tech firms to Miami, countering the perception that companies are only establishing small satellite offices in the region. The move follows recent high-profile residential acquisitions in South Florida by Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin.

data_points.notable_features: Located in Miami's financial district.
data_points.project_notes: Expansion from a previous 10,000 square feet at the same location.

articles.title: Landmaxxing: Billionaire David MacNeil adds to Manalapan compound with $36M buy
articles.narrative: Billionaire David MacNeil, founder of WeatherTech, has expanded his Manalapan compound with the acquisition of a neighboring 1.9-acre property for $36 million. This purchase adds to MacNeil's contiguous land holdings, which now total 5.8 acres, as he continues to assemble a larger estate in the area. The sellers, Ralph and Mary Gesualdo, nearly tripled their investment on the property, which they had acquired in 2020.

data_points.notable_features: The property includes eight bedrooms, nine and a half bathrooms, a guest house, a beach house, and private beach access.
data_points.project_notes: The sellers, Ralph and Mary Gesualdo, purchased the property for $10.3 million in 2020. David MacNeil has spent a total of $136.3 million on three properties in the area since February.

articles.title: Oak Brook mansion relisted for $10M, could fetch highest village price if sold
articles.narrative: A luxury mansion in Oak Brook, IL, has been relisted for just under $10 million. If sold near its asking price, the 15,820-square-foot residence at 404 Fox Trail Lane would set a new record for the highest home sale in the village, surpassing the previous record set in 2003. The property, built in 2009, features seven bedrooms, 13.5 bathrooms, and a range of high-end amenities.

data_points.address: 404 Fox Trail Lane, Oak Brook, IL
data_points.notable_features: Features a brick and limestone exterior, grand motor court, columns in the entrance, a master bedroom with a private sitting room, sauna, steam room, wine cellar, plunge pool, and a five-car garage.
data_points.project_notes: Previously listed for approximately $12 million three years prior.

articles.market_intelligence: The wider Chicago area is experiencing a fast-moving housing market due to limited inventory, leading buyers to act more quickly and spend more.

articles.title: Two St. Charles senior living communities trade for $74M as hot streak continues
articles.narrative: Two senior living communities in St. Charles, IL, were sold for a combined total of $74 million, continuing a strong trend in the Chicago-area senior living market. Preservation Equity Fund Advisors acquired the 108-unit Carroll Tower for $23.5 million from 3 Diamond Development Group, which was facing foreclosure on the property. Separately, National Healthcare Properties purchased The River Glen of St. Charles for $40 million from Citrine Investment Group, which specializes in repositioning distressed senior living assets.

data_points.project_notes: Carroll Tower was facing foreclosure due to a matured $20 million mortgage. Citrine Investment Group acquired The River Glen of St. Charles in 2023 for $19 million with a $13 million mortgage.

articles.title: Lender selling foreclosed Tribune Tower condo of exec tied to Loretto Hospital embezzlement scheme
articles.narrative: A luxury condominium in Chicago's historic Tribune Tower is being marketed for sale by US Bank after its previous owner, Sameer Suhail, forfeited the property in a court-ordered sale. Suhail, a medical supply vendor for Loretto Hospital, was indicted on federal charges related to an alleged $15 million fraudulent billing scheme. The 3,500-square-foot unit, located on the 20th floor, is expected to sell for less than the $4.3 million Suhail paid in 2023.

data_points.notable_features: Located on the 20th floor, featuring a balcony facing the Chicago River and ornate Gothic-style windows.
data_points.project_notes: The unit was previously sold for $4.69 million in 2021 before Suhail's 2023 purchase. The Tribune Tower was redeveloped into luxury condos and retail space by CIM Group and Golub & Company after the Chicago Tribune moved out in 2018.

articles.title: From distressed debt to apartments: Envoi locks in $64M Fortress loan for LaSalle office to resi conversion
articles.narrative: Envoi Partners secured a $64 million construction loan from Fortress Investment Group for the adaptive reuse of a 16-story office building at 19 South LaSalle Street in downtown Chicago. The financing package, which includes senior debt, federal historic tax credits, and private capital, will facilitate the conversion of 207,000 square feet of office space into 207 apartments and 6,811 square feet of ground-floor retail. This project, expected to be completed in 15 months, is a significant step in the revitalization of the LaSalle Street corridor, transforming a historic building into modern residential and retail space.

data_points.notable_features: Historic 132-year-old building designed by William Le Baron Jenney, granted landmark status in December, with ground-floor retail fronting LaSalle Street and Arcade Alley.
data_points.project_notes: Envoi Partners acquired the building's loan note for $4.2 million in October 2024 and assumed ownership for the apartment rebuild. The project received a fee waiver for its permit.

articles.title: Prime Finance buys Jonathan Holtzman’s East Loop apartments for $59M, ending legal fight
articles.narrative: An affiliate of Prime Finance acquired the 190-unit MDA Apartments in Chicago's East Loop for $59 million, resolving a two-year foreclosure lawsuit against the previous owner, City Club Apartments. The transaction effectively dismissed a $69 million debt owed on a $66 million mortgage, with the lender accepting a discount to take ownership of the property. The building had faced operational issues, including broken boilers and an elevator, leading to a court-appointed receiver stabilizing the asset prior to the sale.

data_points.project_notes: The property was previously collateral for a $66 million mortgage originated in 2022. A receiver was appointed in early 2025 due to operational issues including non-working boilers, a broken elevator, and rooftop safety concerns.

articles.market_intelligence: Chicago's multifamily market is experiencing strong rent growth, with effective rents increasing 3.2% year-over-year as of Q2 2026, attributed to a historically low new supply pipeline. This contrasts with the reluctance of lenders to take over distressed office properties in the Cook County court system.

articles.title: BlackRock, MGX investing $5B into Aligned Data Centers to supercharge growth
articles.narrative: A joint venture between BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners and Abu Dhabi-based MGX is investing $5 billion into Aligned Data Centers, a Plano-based firm they recently acquired from Macquarie Asset Management for $40 billion. This significant capital injection is intended to fuel Aligned's expansion of its data center capacity across the Americas, including key markets like Dallas and Atlanta. The acquisition and subsequent investment highlight the intense demand for data center infrastructure driven by the power requirements of generative AI and other artificial intelligence technologies, prompting a race among global tech companies, sovereign wealth funds, and investment firms to expand or acquire existing data center properties.

data_points.notable_features: Operates and plans data centers across the Americas, including Dallas, Atlanta, Chile, Brazil, and Mexico, with over 6.4 GW in operational and planned output capacity. Boasts 50 campuses and 78 data centers either under construction or operational as of October.
data_points.project_notes: The $5 billion investment is primarily for expanding capacity.

articles.market_intelligence: The power requirements of generative AI and other artificial intelligence ventures are rapidly increasing the valuations of existing data center properties. Communities are concerned about rising electric bills and environmental impacts like wastewater usage due to data center developments. In Texas, there are concerns about the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) grid capacity, leading Governor Greg Abbott to call for a ban on data center developments in rural areas and recommend statewide regulations.

articles.title: McShane secures $79M loan to pay off construction debt on East Dallas apartments
articles.narrative: Conor Commercial Real Estate, a subsidiary of The McShane Companies, has secured a $78.7 million construction takeout loan for its recently completed multifamily project, The Flynn at Live Oak, in East Dallas. The financing will be used to pay off the original construction debt on the 327-unit apartment building. The project, which faced challenges in a market with rising interest rates and increased supply, is offering significant concessions to new renters.

data_points.notable_features: Amenities include a pool, sky lounge, gym, coworking space, and fire pits.
data_points.project_notes: The project was originally expected to cost $50 million and be completed by March 2024. The building is offering two months of free rent to new tenants.

articles.market_intelligence: Multifamily developers in North Texas have faced challenges stabilizing apartment buildings due to rising interest rates and a significant increase in new apartment supply, which has led to downward pressure on rents. Old East Dallas, a neighborhood approximately 3 miles from downtown, has seen a surge in multifamily development interest, contrasting with its past reputation as a high-crime area.

articles.title: Texas construction report: Eli Lilly tops permit list with $378M in filings for ‘Project Houston’
articles.narrative: Eli Lilly is investing $378 million to construct a new manufacturing facility in Houston, Texas, dedicated to producing ingredients for its GLP-1 pill. The project, dubbed 'Project Houston,' involves five buildings totaling nearly 700,000 square feet, with initial completion expected between summer and winter 2027 and full completion by 2030. This significant investment underscores the pharmaceutical company's commitment to expanding its production capabilities for a key product.

data_points.project_notes: Permits filed for five buildings.

articles.title: Foxconn to pour $72M into Apple AI server manufacturing facility in Houston
articles.narrative: Foxconn, a Taiwanese electronics manufacturer, is investing $71.9 million to expand its AI server manufacturing facility in Houston, TX. The project, located at 8718 Fairbanks North Houston Road, will add over 74,000 square feet of production area, offices, and a break room, with completion expected in early 2027. This expansion builds on Foxconn's 2025 acquisition of the buildings for $142 million, which are leased to its subsidiary, Q-Edge, for the production of AI servers and motherboards for Apple data centers.

data_points.address: 8718 Fairbanks North Houston Road, Houston, TX
data_points.project_notes: An affiliate of Foxconn previously acquired the buildings for $142 million in 2025 and leased them to Q-Edge.

articles.market_intelligence: Texas is becoming a hub for AI manufacturing and data centers, with a report suggesting it could have the most data centers in the nation by 2030. Major investments include Elon Musk's projects in Austin and Central Texas, Meta's $10 billion data center in El Paso, and Project Big Pine in Texarkana. Governor Greg Abbott has recently advocated for state-level regulations and a ban on data center developments in rural communities, a shift from his previous pro-development stance.

articles.title: Sasha Bass steps down as CEO of Fort Worth’s Sundance Square amid ongoing criticism of her management
articles.narrative: Sasha Bass is stepping down as CEO of Sundance Square, a prominent 37-block mixed-use district in downtown Fort Worth, after a five-year tenure marked by efforts to expand the company's operational scope and increase foot traffic through live events. Former Fort Worth Police Chief Ed Kraus, who joined Sundance Square in 2019 and became vice president in 2020, will succeed her as president and CEO on September 1. Bass's leadership faced criticism regarding high rents and a perceived lack of effective retail and restaurant revitalization post-pandemic, leading to significant storefront vacancies. In a strategic shift, Sundance Square recently engaged JLL to manage retail leasing and LanCarte Commercial for office properties, moving away from its previous in-house leasing approach.

data_points.notable_features: 37-block downtown district with retail and office properties.
data_points.project_notes: Sasha Bass was appointed CEO in 2019. Ed Kraus will take over as CEO on September 1.

articles.title: More CIM-owned offices in Bay Area headed for foreclosure after loan default, receivership
articles.narrative: Lenders are initiating foreclosure proceedings on CIM Group's Central Tower in San Francisco, following a default on a $98 million loan. The historic two-building office property, located at 703 Market Street and 30 Third Street, was placed into receivership in May after its largest tenant vacated, leading to a significant drop in occupancy. This situation highlights the ongoing challenges in the Bay Area office market, with lenders now exploring options to take ownership or sell the asset to recover the outstanding debt.

data_points.address: 703 Market Street and 30 Third Street, San Francisco, CA
data_points.notable_features: Historic buildings, formerly known as the Call Building, once the tallest building west of Chicago.
data_points.project_notes: Property previously acquired by CIM Group in 2013 for approximately $50 million and underwent $47.5 million in renovations. Refinanced in 2019 with the $98 million loan.

articles.title: Amazon grabs Sunnyvale offices once occupied by Google at Jay Paul Co. campus
articles.narrative: Amazon has expanded its presence at the Moffett Towers complex in Sunnyvale, signing a lease for the entire 317,000-square-foot building at 1000 Enterprise Way. This space was previously occupied by Google, which had been gradually vacating its offices at the campus. The deal reflects a potential shift in the Silicon Valley office market, with large tech companies showing renewed confidence and increasing their office footprints.

data_points.project_notes: Amazon previously leased 1140 and 1160 Enterprise Way at the same campus.

articles.market_intelligence: The first half of 2026 was the strongest first-six-months period for office leasing in Silicon Valley since 2018. Sizable leases over 100,000 square feet have doubled from the 2025 average. AI firms have leased 2.4 million square feet of offices in Silicon Valley and the Peninsula this year. New office construction has dropped to its lowest level in over two decades.

articles.title: CIM defaults on Kaiser HQ tower as office distress in Oakland spreads
articles.narrative: CIM Group is facing a potential foreclosure on its $97.1 million loan for 1 Kaiser Plaza, a 28-story office tower in Oakland, after the property's value plummeted to $53.5 million from $212 million in 2016. The loan entered special servicing in October 2024 following a significant downsizing by the largest tenant, Kaiser Permanente, which reduced its headquarters footprint by one-third. Despite CIM Group remaining current on interest payments, the lender has demanded immediate repayment and placed the property's income in trust, highlighting the widespread distress in the Oakland office market.

data_points.project_notes: Loan issued in 2016. Property value fell from $212 million in 2016 to $53.5 million. Loan entered special servicing in October 2024.

articles.market_intelligence: Oakland's office market has approximately one-third vacancy. Distressed office properties in the East Bay are selling for fractions of their previous values or being returned to lenders. Heitman Capital Management seized ownership of the Clorox Building at 1221 Broadway in a foreclosure proceeding last month.

articles.title: Original Developer Trades Castro Valley Multifamily Duo
articles.narrative: Berkadia has facilitated the sale and acquisition financing of two adjacent multifamily properties in Castro Valley, California, totaling 135 units. The Cedars, an 83-unit community, sold for $21.45 million, while the 52-unit Creekside Terrace fetched $14.1 million. The properties, which offer significant value-add potential, were sold by their original developer and longtime owner, Felson Companies, to Prime Residential. The transaction highlights strong investor demand for rare, long-held assets in the Bay Area, despite a complex market environment.

data_points.notable_features: Two neighboring multifamily communities with value-add potential.
data_points.project_notes: Properties held by a single owner for over 50 years.

articles.title: Resorts World NYC Adds 1,400 Slot Machines as Part of $5.5B Expansion
articles.narrative: Resorts World New York City has opened the first floor of its commercial casino, adding 1,400 slot machines and bringing the total onsite to 3,900. This expansion is part of a larger $5.5 billion development plan for the site, which is expected to significantly boost gross gaming revenue and tax contributions to New York State. The initial slot machines have already generated over $230 million in gross gaming revenue in 11 weeks, indicating strong public demand.

data_points.phase_1: 1,400 slot machines added, bringing total to 3,900
data_points.total_project_all_phases: 350,000-square-foot gaming floor with 6,000 slot machines and 800 live table games, a 7,000-seat entertainment venue, 2,000 hotel rooms and more than 10 acres of public green space

articles.title: Calare Acquires Industrial in Boston’s Hyde Park Neighborhood
articles.narrative: Calare Properties has acquired One Westinghouse Plaza Building K, a 42,000-square-foot industrial warehouse/flex condominium in Boston's Hyde Park neighborhood. The property is part of a larger 22-acre industrial and mixed-use campus. The new owner plans to implement a capital improvement program and pursue a long-term leasing strategy for the available space, capitalizing on the scarcity of quality industrial space in the Boston market.

data_points.notable_features: Part of a 22-acre, 10-building industrial and mixed-use site with a manufacturing history dating back to the early 1900s.
data_points.project_notes: The building is nearly 50% leased to a long-term tenant. The new ownership is executing a capital improvement plan.

articles.title: Fresno Apartments Fetch $44M in First-Ever Sale
articles.narrative: The Mogharebi Group represented JBT Property Management in the sale of Maroa Park Apartments, a 248-unit multifamily community in Fresno, to a private buyer for $44 million. This transaction marks the first time the property has been on the market since its construction in 1986, offering the buyer a rare opportunity to acquire a well-maintained, large-scale asset directly from its original owner. The acquisition is expected to enhance the buyer's regional presence and improve operational efficiency without requiring significant capital investment, capitalizing on the property's immediate income upside and strong market fundamentals in the Central Valley.

data_points.notable_features: First-time-on-the-market property since its construction in 1986, acquired directly from original ownership.

articles.title: Want To Weigh In On The Next Opportunity Zone Maps? You May Be Too Late
articles.narrative: The second iteration of the Opportunity Zone program, established by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, is nearing its final mapping phase, with governors preparing to submit their proposed census tracts to the Treasury Department by September 28. This new version, OZ 2.0, aims to narrow the focus of tax incentives to lower-income and rural areas, reducing the number of eligible zones from 8,764 to an estimated 6,544. While many states have already completed their public input processes for nominations, the uneven rollout across states may disadvantage smaller communities lacking resources to propose their tracts. Experts emphasize the importance of state leaders actively educating and engaging rural areas to ensure their participation in the program.

data_points.project_notes: The Opportunity Zone 2.0 program, passed into law with the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, reduces the number of opportunity zones from 8,764 to an estimated 6,544, with an emphasis on lower-income and rural communities.

articles.title: AI-Assisted Construction-Bid Startup Fields $4M Seed Investment
articles.narrative: Guthrie AI, a Philadelphia-based startup leveraging AI and a global workforce to streamline construction bidding, has successfully closed a $4 million seed funding round. The company's platform, which is currently 10% automated, aims to help specialty contractors increase their bidding capacity by up to 70% per person. The investment will primarily be used to expand its engineering team in the U.S. and further develop its proprietary AI platform, which currently relies on human input for complex tasks like interpreting construction documents.

articles.title: BlackRock Finances $12B Meta Data Center, Closes Aligned Acquisition
articles.narrative: BlackRock has significantly expanded its presence in the artificial intelligence data center market by orchestrating two major transactions totaling approximately $57 billion. The firm is leading a $12 billion debt financing for a new Meta data center campus in El Paso, Texas, where BlackRock holds an 80% joint venture stake. Concurrently, BlackRock's subsidiary Global Infrastructure Partners, in partnership with MGX, finalized the $40 billion acquisition of data center provider Aligned Data Centers from Macquarie Asset Management, with an additional $5 billion investment planned for expansion. These moves underscore BlackRock's strategic positioning as a dominant force in hyperscale data center development and financing.

data_points.notable_features: Expected to have close to 1 gigawatt of capacity.
data_points.project_notes: Developed through a joint venture where BlackRock owns an 80% stake and Meta owns 20%.

articles.title: Grubb Properties Merges Funds To Create $1.9B Apartment REIT
articles.narrative: Grubb Properties has consolidated several legacy funds into a newly formed, non-traded multifamily REIT called Link Apartments REIT, valued at approximately $1.9 billion. This strategic move, which includes a $617 million recapitalization of over 60 properties, aims to create a larger balance sheet for enhanced financing capabilities and improve operational simplicity and efficiency. The portfolio comprises more than 5,600 apartments, including the under-construction 8 Carlisle Street tower in Manhattan. Concurrently, Grubb secured a $240 million credit facility for its separate Link Apartments Opportunity Zone REIT and a $300 million senior construction loan along with a $77 million mezzanine loan to fully capitalize the 8 Carlisle project.

articles.market_intelligence: Second-quarter apartment absorption reached 124,600 units, one of the highest in 25 years, contributing to lower vacancy rates. A slowdown in new housing construction is also providing a tailwind for multifamily developers.

articles.title: GSA Head Says Federal Government Has 'Place To Play' In Southwest D.C. Redevelopment
articles.narrative: The head of the General Services Administration (GSA) indicated that the federal government plans to take a more active role in the redevelopment of 250 acres in Southwest D.C., situated between the National Mall and the waterfront. This marks a shift from the GSA's previous strategy of selling federally owned properties individually without a master plan. Administrator Ed Forst suggested the government could act as a "first mover" to catalyze the transformation, potentially using models like the successful redevelopment of The Yards in Southeast D.C. This new approach, emphasizing collaboration with stakeholders, aims to accelerate the revitalization of the corridor, addressing concerns about the loss of government control over significant real estate.

data_points.notable_features: The 250-acre redevelopment area is located between the National Mall and D.C.'s southwest waterfront.
data_points.project_notes: The GSA previously offloaded the nearly 1M SF Regional Office Building at Seventh and D streets SW to Dalian Development, and the L-shaped Liberty Loan building to Satvik Raj.
